newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq calls Bill Clinton ignorant "womaniser".
newsitem.headline: Iraq calls Bill Clinton ignorant "womaniser".

text.p: Iraq's official media heaped scorn on President Bill Clinton on Friday, calling him an ignorant "womaniser".

"It seems Clinton has not learned a lesson from his criminal predecessor (former U.S. President) George Bush," declared the ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra. Bush was president during the 1991 Gulf War that ousted Iraqi troops from Kuwait.
"He (Bush) thought arrogant use of power will provide the keys to control Iraq. He failed and has gone and Iraq and its victorious leader still survive," the paper said.
"The truth is that the country whose inexperienced president is a womaniser...is ignorant of what is taking place in the world."
The paper said Clinton and his advisers should have known that their anti-Iraq coalition was crumbling.
European support from some countries was muted for the cruise missile attacks, which came after Iraqi troops intervened to support a Kurdish faction fighting another Kurdish group in northern Iraq.

The government-controlled newspapers reiterated in their commentaries that Baghdad would continue resisting violation by U.S. and allied planes of its airspace but did not say how and when that would happen.

U.S., British and French warplanes patrol two no-fly zones over Iraq, one in the south and the other in the north. Washington has extended the southern air-exclusion zone almost to the outskirts of the Iraqi capital Baghdad but France has said it will only patrol along the original zone.

On Thursday, Iraq's all powerful Revolutionary Command Council (RCC), following a meeting chaired by President Saddam Hussein, issued a statement saying "America's aggression" was continuing but it fell short of ordering attacks on the intruding planes.

The papers published a picture of Saddam meeting his Defence Minister General Sultan Hashim Ahmed, commander of Iraq's elite forces, the Republican Guards, as well as senior air defence officers. No details of the meeting were given.
Iraq's dinar, a barometre of Baghdad's relations with the U.N. Security Council and the United States, gained back value that it lost to the dollar during the crisis.
The dinar on Friday rose to 1,100 to the U.S. dollar from about 1,750 in mid week.

Moslem preachers poured their wrath on Clinton on Friday and and one of them pleaded with the Almighty to punish him "for all the crimes he has committed against our country, the land of believers, and fling him into the blazing fires of hell after death."
